Priorities & Progress

What is being tracked, what this office can actually do about it, what the district controls, the evidence behind it, and when it is next updated.

A commissioner is one vote of nine on a board that acts together. Where an outcome depends on the full Board, on district administration or on school leadership, that is stated rather than claimed.

During his campaign, T. L. Harris called his early-reading commitment “The Third Grade Standard.” That wording is kept here as history, not as a current promise. Each priority shows where the subject stands today.

Accountability at a glance

8Not Started

Statuses are listed in their fixed order. The order is not a ranking of how things are going.

Current priorities

Early Literacy

Not Started

Early Literacy and Third-Grade Reading

Third-grade reading proficiency across Memphis-Shelby County Schools, and what the Board asks about it.

“Increase third-grade reading proficiency by 10% within two academic years.”

Campaign wording, kept as historical context. It is not a current commitment or a predicted outcome.

What he controlsHow he votes on items that come before the Board. What he asks for in Board meetings and puts on the public record. What he reports back to District 6.

What depends on the districtReading outcomes depend on classroom instruction, school leadership and district-wide programs. The Board acts as a body, and any single commissioner's vote is one of nine.

Not Started

Early Literacy Instruction and Structured Literacy

How reading is taught in the early grades, and which instructional approach the district uses.

“Expand structured literacy practices across all K-3 classrooms.”

Campaign wording, kept as historical context. It is not a current commitment or a predicted outcome.

What he controlsHow he votes on curriculum and budget items that reach the Board. What he asks about instructional practice in public session.

What depends on the districtCurriculum selection and teacher training are run by district administration. A commissioner does not set classroom practice.

Student Achievement

Not Started

Early Intervention

How quickly students who fall behind are identified, and what support follows.

“Prioritize early intervention before grade retention becomes necessary.”

Campaign wording, kept as historical context. It is not a current commitment or a predicted outcome.

What he controlsHow he votes on programs and funding that come before the Board. What he asks about identification and support in public session.

What depends on the districtIdentification and support happen at school level, under district programs. Some requirements come from outside the district.

Not Started

School Improvement Goals

School improvement goals: what they are, who sets them, and how the Board oversees progress against them.

“Require every District 6 school to publish annual measurable improvement goals.”

Campaign wording, kept as historical context. It is not a current commitment or a predicted outcome.

Improvement goals are how a district states publicly what it is trying to change.

What he controlsHow he votes on goals and plans presented to the Board. What he asks for in the way of progress reporting.

What depends on the districtGoals are set and carried out by district and school leadership. The Board's role is oversight, exercised as a body.

Safe & Supportive Schools

Not Started

Safe and Supportive Learning Environments

School climate, behavioral standards, and the support available to students and staff.

“Reduce classroom disruptions by 15% within two years through clear behavioral standards. Every student deserves a learning environment where they feel secure, supported, and ready to learn.”

Campaign wording, kept as historical context. It is not a current commitment or a predicted outcome.

What he controlsHow he votes on policy that comes before the Board. What he raises publicly about school conditions in District 6.

What depends on the districtDay-to-day discipline and safety are handled by school leadership under district policy. A commissioner does not manage staff or individual student matters.

Accountability & Stewardship

Not Started

Annual Literacy Growth Reports

Whether literacy growth is reported publicly each year, and in a form residents can find and read.

“Publish annual literacy growth reports for District 6 schools, and host quarterly public updates to ensure transparency and accountability.”

Campaign wording, kept as historical context. It is not a current commitment or a predicted outcome.

A commitment nobody reports on cannot be checked by anyone.

What he controlsWhat he asks the district to report. What he publishes to District 6 through this site, whether or not the district publishes its own.

What depends on the districtDistrict-wide reporting is produced by the administration. What this office can do on its own is publish what it has, and say plainly what it does not have.

Not Started

Public Performance Dashboard

Whether district performance information is published in one place the public can find and use.

“Launch a publicly accessible quarterly performance dashboard within the first year of service.”

Campaign wording, kept as historical context. It is not a current commitment or a predicted outcome.

Information the public cannot find cannot hold anyone to account.

What he controlsWhat this office publishes and keeps current on this site.

What depends on the districtA district-wide dashboard would be built and maintained by the district. Any figure shown here must come from a published district or state source, with that source named.

Family & Community Engagement

Not Started

Quarterly Town Halls

Regular public meetings in District 6 where residents can raise concerns directly.

“Host quarterly District 6 town halls and publish meeting summaries within 10 business days.”

Campaign wording, kept as historical context. It is not a current commitment or a predicted outcome.

Residents need a predictable place to raise something and be answered in public.

What he controlsWhether the meetings are scheduled and held. Whether a summary is published afterwards. What follow-up is recorded.

What depends on the districtHolding the meetings is within this office's own control. Attendance, and what the district does in response to what is raised, are not.

How progress is measured

This is a record of work, not a scorecard. It is written so that a reader can check it rather than take it on trust.

Status

Every priority carries one of five values: Not Started, Monitoring, In Progress, Completed, or On Hold. There is no status that means going well. Not Started means that nothing has been recorded here yet. It does not say that no work has happened.

Baseline and target

A figure appears only when it comes from a published source, and that source is named. Where no baseline exists, the page says so instead of estimating one.

Evidence

Where a document, dataset or official record supports an entry, the entry links to it and shows the date it was last checked. Where none is recorded, the entry says so.

Control

Each priority separates what a commissioner directly controls from what he can influence and what depends on the district. One commissioner is one vote of nine on a board that acts together.

Next update

Where the office has set a date for the next review, the entry shows it, so a reader can tell the difference between steady work and a page nobody has touched. Where none is set, the entry says so.

No progress bar without a source

A progress figure is shown only where a real baseline, a current value and a target all exist and the source of those figures is linked. Otherwise there is nothing to draw.

Sources: MSCS Board of Education; T. L. Harris campaign platform, voteharris901.com (campaign wording only).
